message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 192, "amount_cents": 3148}, {"order_id": 193, "amount_cents": 9581}, {"order_id": 194, "amount_cents": 5972}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, with the same three order IDs and amounts. Next I'll check the orders list to confirm the refunds reference real orders before computing balances.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order, so the refund work looks consistent. I'll get the net balance for acme, the first of the three customers.
Acme's net balance of 33841 matches my check: orders 190 and 193 total 43422, less the 9581 refund on order 193. Refunds are verified against the ledger, so I'll get birch's net balance next.
Birch's net balance of 34692 matches my check: orders 191 and 194 total 40664, less the 5972 refund on order 194. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get their net balance next.

All three net balances match my own check against the orders and the ledger's refunds, and the ledger matches Alpha's handoff. Refund work looks complete and correct, so I'll record the first payout, acme for 33841 cents.

Acme's payout is recorded. I re-checked all three balances against the orders and refunds, and they agree: birch is 26465+14199-5972=34692 and cobalt is 19506+2421-3148=18779. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's balance of 18779 matches my check: orders 192 and 195 total 21927, less the 3148 refund on order 192. This is the last payout, so I'll record it.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my independent check against the orders and the ledger's refunds, so the batch is complete.
